The workshop runs over **three days** in the conference room of **Knight Campus Building 2** at the University of Oregon: **Wednesday, June 10** and **Thursday, June 11** (10:00 am – 12:00 pm and 2:00 – 4:00 pm each day), and **Friday, June 12** (10:00 am – 12:00 pm, followed by a **working lunch — food provided — 12:00 – 1:30 pm**). An **optional Day 0** runs the day before (**Tuesday, June 9**) for participants who want a refresher on R, the Unix command line, and getting their laptop set up (RStudio + packages) before the workshop proper begins. Day 0 is offered as **two identical sessions — 10:00 am – 12:00 pm and 3:00 – 5:00 pm — and you only need to attend one.**

::: callout-tip
**Before Day 1:** complete the [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) on the laptop you'll bring. Plan 30–60 minutes, the day before — *not* the morning of.
:::

::: callout-note
The tables below list each day's sessions in order, grouped into the scheduled **morning (10–12)** and **afternoon (2–4)** blocks. The plan is intensive; any session that runs long carries over into the self-paced materials rather than displacing the rest of the day.
:::

## Day 0 (optional) — Software Setup & Computational Refresher

Offered on **Tuesday, June 9** (same room) as **two identical sessions** — **10:00 am – 12:00 pm** and **3:00 – 5:00 pm**. **You only need to attend one;** come to whichever fits your schedule. Both sessions cover the same material, so **drop in for the parts you need** and bring your laptop along with any install problems you couldn't solve on your own.

Each session covers, as time and demand allow:

| Topic | Material |
|---|---|
| Laptop setup help — R, RStudio, the workshop dataset | [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) |
| Installing R / Bioconductor packages in R & RStudio | [Tutorial 00](Exercise_Folder/Tutorial_00_Setup_RStudio_Packages.html) |
| R fundamentals refresher — tidyverse, writing functions | [Appendix A](Resources_Folder/Appendix_A_R_Programming.html) |
| Unix command line — `cd`, `ls`, pipes, `grep`, `wget` | [Appendix B](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html), [Appendix F](Resources_Folder/Appendix_F_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) |

## Bonus tracks — self-paced after the workshop

The following modules are **not part of the three-day in-person workshop**. They ship alongside the workshop materials for you to work through on your own time once you've finished the core sequence:

- **Lecture 09 + Tutorial 09** — Bulk and single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac
- **Lecture 10 + Tutorial 10** — WGCNA on bulk RNA-seq
- **Lecture 11 + Tutorial 11** — Spatial transcriptomics with Visium
- **Lecture 12 + Tutorial 12** — Trajectory inference & cell–cell communication
- **Lecture 13 + Tutorial 13** — FAIR principles and data submission
- **[Full Talapas RNA-seq run from raw FASTQs](Additional_Resources.qmd)** — the entire pipeline on UO's HPC starting from raw reads and Cell Ranger, on a real 10x dataset (in Additional Resources)

## Materials

The full **lecture ↔ reading ↔ tutorial ↔ Talapas** crosswalk — every topic's slide deck, book chapter, laptop tutorial, and matching Talapas script — lives on the **[Materials](Materials.qmd)** page in the navbar.

## What to bring

- A laptop with at least **16 GB RAM** and **~10 GB free disk**
- R ≥ 4.4 and RStudio Desktop installed (see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd))
- The workshop dataset downloaded and unpacked (the setup script handles this)
- A power adapter — outlets are limited in the conference room

## During-workshop support

The instructors will be in the room throughout the workshop. For questions outside workshop hours, email is the most reliable channel — see the [About](about.qmd) page.
